speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me how long you've had this painful ulcer on your leg and do you have any history of diabetes or peripheral vascular disease?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and the lesion starting at an insect bite site, does the ulcer have raised, violaceous borders, and have you noticed any similar skin issues elsewhere? I would also like to check if you have any joint pain or eye redness currently.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of an ant bite triggering this painful ulcer with violaceous borders, combined with your history of Crohn's disease and anterior uveitis, is highly suggestive of Pyoderma Gangrenosum. REQUEST TEST: Biopsy of the ulcer edge.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Skin Biopsy Histopathology: Neutrophilic infiltration without infection, consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you, the biopsy confirms the diagnosis. I will now proceed with a treatment plan to manage the inflammation and promote healing. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum
